stages.name: Native lands
stages.desc: Libyan (later Numidian), Iberian, Italic and island peoples

stages.name: Tyre's homeland
stages.desc: Tyre, Sidon and the Phoenician coast

stages.name: Tyrian foundation
stages.desc: Settlements and trading posts founded from Tyre

stages.name: Carthage's early sphere
stages.desc: Carthage and the lands it leads in the west

stages.name: Greek colonies
stages.desc: Cities founded by Greek settlers in the west

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Tyrian Kition, around a temple of Astarte, among the island's Cypriot kingdoms
The kings of Cyprus submit to Sargon II; his stele is set up at Kition

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Island Tyre, city of King Pygmalion, leads the trade of Phoenicia
King Hiram II of Tyre pays tribute to Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria
King Luli of Tyre and Sidon flees Sennacherib's army to Cyprus
Esarhaddon of Assyria destroys Sidon
Assyria besieges island Tyre and takes its mainland territory

states.name: Spain
timeline: Tartessian lands of the south; Phoenician traders already at Huelva
Tyrian Gadir (Cádiz) trades for the silver of Tartessos
Carthaginians settle Ebusus on Ibiza, by Diodorus's date

states.name: Libya
timeline: Libyan peoples of the coast and the desert
Phoenicians begin to settle at Lepcis on the Tripolitanian coast

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Libyan farmers and herders; Tyrians may already trade at Utica
Traditional date: Elissa's Tyrians found Qart-hadasht by the Byrsa hill
The earliest excavated houses and pottery at Carthage (Bir Massouda, Byrsa)
Carthage has grown into the largest Phoenician city of the west

states.name: Italy
timeline: Italic, Etruscan, Sicel and Nuragic Sard peoples; Phoenician traders call on Sardinia
Phoenicians settle Sulcis on Sardinia; Greeks trade from Pithekoussai
Greeks found Naxos and Syracuse: the colonisation of Sicily and southern Italy begins
Greek Sybaris in the south; Phoenician Motya in western Sicily
Greeks found Selinus, close to the Phoenician west of Sicily

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Libyan peoples, ancestors of the later Numidians
Phoenician traders on the islet of Rachgoun off the western coast

states.name: Malta
timeline: Farming villages of the Maltese islands; Phoenician ships call
Phoenicians settle, with a sanctuary of Astarte at Tas-Silġ

events.title: Pygmalion's reign
events.text: Pygmalion (Pumayyaton) becomes king of Tyre; he will reign for forty-seven years, according to Menander of Ephesus.

events.title: Utica
events.text: Ancient writers call Utica older than Carthage, and excavations there have found Phoenician pottery of the 9th century.

events.title: Huelva
events.text: Phoenician pottery found at Huelva shows Levantine traders in Tartessos by the 9th century.

events.title: Acherbas murdered
events.text: Pygmalion has his sister Elissa's husband Acherbas, priest of Melqart, killed for his gold.

events.title: Elissa's flight
events.text: Elissa sails from Tyre by night with the gold and a band of nobles; Josephus dates it to Pygmalion's seventh year.

events.title: Stop at Kition
events.text: On Cyprus, a high priest joins the exiles and eighty young women are taken aboard as wives, says Justin.

events.title: The ox-hide
events.text: The Libyans sell as much land as an ox-hide can cover; Elissa cuts it into thin strips and encircles the Byrsa hill.

events.title: Qart-hadasht
events.text: Timaeus's date for the founding of the 'new city', thirty-eight years before the first Olympiad.

events.title: Rent to the Libyans
events.text: The settlers pay a yearly rent for their land to the Libyans, a payment Carthage made for centuries.

events.title: Elissa's pyre
events.text: Pressed to marry the Libyan king Iarbas, Elissa climbs a pyre and kills herself, says Justin.

events.title: Gadir
events.text: The oldest layers of Phoenician Cádiz date from around 800; Gadir trades for Tartessian silver.

events.title: Nora stone
events.text: A Phoenician inscription from Nora in Sardinia, among the oldest in the west, names a temple and perhaps Tarshish.

events.title: First Olympiad
events.text: The first Olympic Games: the fixed point from which Timaeus counted back to Carthage's founding.

events.title: Pithekoussai
events.text: Euboean Greeks settle on Ischia, trading with Etruscans and Phoenicians.

events.title: Sulcis
events.text: Phoenicians found Sulcis on the island of Sant'Antioco off Sardinia.

events.title: Bir Massouda
events.text: Carthage's oldest excavated layers: Phoenician and Greek pottery and bones radiocarbon-dated to the late 9th or 8th century.

events.title: Rome
events.text: The traditional founding date of Rome, a village of the Latins on the Tiber.

events.title: Tas-Silġ
events.text: Phoenicians on Malta take over an old temple site and dedicate it to Astarte.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: Phoenicians trade at Lixus on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

events.title: Cumae
events.text: Greeks from Pithekoussai found Cumae on the Italian mainland.

events.title: Tribute to Assyria
events.text: Hiram II of Tyre pays tribute to the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III.

events.title: Naxos
events.text: Greeks from Chalcis found Naxos, the first Greek colony on Sicily.

events.title: Syracuse
events.text: Corinthian settlers found Syracuse on the island of Ortygia.

events.title: The tophet
events.text: The first urns are buried in Carthage's sacred precinct of Baal Hammon and Tanit, holding the burned remains of infants and animals.

events.title: Megara Hyblaea
events.text: Greeks from Megara settle on the east coast of Sicily.

events.title: Motya
events.text: Phoenicians settle the island of Motya off western Sicily.

events.title: Sybaris
events.text: Achaean Greeks found Sybaris, soon famous for its wealth.

events.title: Croton
events.text: Achaeans found Croton on the Gulf of Taranto.

events.title: Sargon's stele
events.text: The kings of Cyprus submit to Assyria; a stele of Sargon II is set up at Kition.

events.title: Taras
events.text: Spartan settlers found Taras, modern Taranto.

events.title: Luli flees
events.text: Sennacherib of Assyria marches on Phoenicia; King Luli flees from Tyre to Cyprus.

events.title: A growing city
events.text: Carthage spreads from the Byrsa slopes toward the shore, with tombs on the hills behind.

events.title: Gela
events.text: Rhodians and Cretans found Gela on the south coast of Sicily.

events.title: Sidon destroyed
events.text: Esarhaddon of Assyria destroys Sidon and executes its king.

events.title: Tyre's treaty
events.text: Esarhaddon imposes a treaty on Baal I of Tyre, controlling its ports and trade.

events.title: Rachgoun
events.text: Phoenician traders settle the islet of Rachgoun off the coast of western Algeria.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Assyria besieges island Tyre and cuts it off from its mainland.

events.title: Ebusus
events.text: Carthaginians found a colony on Ibiza, 160 years after their city's founding, says Diodorus.

events.title: Selinus
events.text: Greeks from Megara Hyblaea found Selinus in western Sicily, by Diodorus's date.

events.title: Lepcis
events.text: Phoenicians begin to settle at Lepcis, later Lepcis Magna, in Tripolitania.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight of today's countries (regions are today's boundaries), by who held the leading coastal settlements in each. A simplification: colonists held only a few harbours, and the interiors stayed native. Carthage appears at Timaeus's traditional date of 814 BC; its earliest excavated layers date from the late 9th or 8th century.
